title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is a curve over a field K; Grothendieck is thinking mainly of X = U_{0,3} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞} over a number field. I ⊂ X_{K̄} is a Γ-stable set of base points, Γ = Gal(K̄/K). π̂_1(X,I) is the profinite fundamental groupoid on these base points. Θ is an automorphism of π̂_1(X,I), a 'virtual Galois element'. The problem is to find necessary, and ideally sufficient, conditions for Θ to come from some u ∈ Γ. Condition 1 is the 'lacets' (inertia/loop) condition, which he calls the most important: Θ sends each inertia loop to a conjugate of its λ-th power, with λ the cyclotomic character.

Condition 2 (completed at the top of this page). For every finite étale cover X' → X defined over K, Θ should lift to an action Θ' on π̂_1(X', I'), where I' = X'|I is the inverse image of I. He notes when the groupoid of X' is usable. X' should be connected as a K-scheme ('K-connexe'), i.e. Γ is transitive on π_0(X'_{K̄}), and I' should meet the relevant components. With a base point x ∈ X_K ∪ I, condition 2 becomes a stability condition: Θ must stabilize the open subgroups of π̂_1(X,x) that correspond to covers defined over K, i.e. the Γ-stable open subgroups.

Condition 3. For K-morphisms f : X' → Y to other curves (not necessarily covers of X) and a K-rational base point x' ∈ X'_K ∩ I', the lifted action Θ' on π̂_1(X',x') must stabilize the kernel of π̂_1(X',x') → π̂_1(Y, f(x')). This is again a stability condition on subgroups, but for a different class of subgroups: the kernels of 'geometric' quotients.

Condition 4. Let X'_1, X'_2 be finite covers of X, and f : X'_1 → X'_2 any K-morphism. Grothendieck stresses, double-underlined, that f need not be an X-morphism. Put I'_i = X'_i|I and J = I'_1 ∩ f^{-1}(I'_2), assumed nonempty. Then the induced groupoid map π̂_1(X'_1, J) → π̂_1(X'_2, I'_2) must be compatible with the extended actions of Θ (up to the indeterminacy discussed in 2).

On the next page he sketches a condition 5 merging 3 and 4, using maps f_1, f_2 to a common Y with f_2 surjective on π_1. He then says that conditions 2–4 are not the truly natural ones. The real goal is necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing the Θ coming from Γ.

In modern terms, this is an attempt to cut the Galois image out of Aut/Out of π̂_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞}) (or of the 'Teichmüller tower'). The method is to demand compatibility with:
- the whole tower of K-defined covers;
- all K-morphisms between covers, including those not over X;
- all K-morphisms to other curves.
This is the same circle of ideas as the GT-relations, Ihara's question, the Oda–Matsumoto conjecture, and Pop's 'finite tripod' variants of I/OM.
errors: Condition 3 as written has π̂_1(X', x) → π̂_1(Y, f(x)), where x' and f(x') are meant (slip of the pen).

The phrase about 'I' ∩ X'_K ≠ ∅ ... il suffit que Γ soit transitif sur π_0(X')' is garbled. Transitivity of Γ on π_0(X'_{K̄}) is the condition for X' to be K-connected. Non-emptiness of I' ∩ X'(K), or I' meeting each geometric component, is a separate requirement on base points; it is not implied by connectedness. The marginal note ('il y a lieu d'exiger ...') seems to correct exactly this point.
Condition 2 for an automorphism Θ given only up to inner conjugation needs care with base points. Grothendieck acknowledges this indeterminacy ('s'il y [a]', 'cf 2.').

ideas.what: Characterize the image of Gal(K̄/K) in automorphisms of π̂_1(U_{0,3}, I) (tangential/rational base points) by intrinsic necessary conditions.
ideas.modern_name: Galois image inside GT / anabelian characterization of G_Q via π̂_1(P^1 \ {0,1,∞})
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (program stated; this list of conditions not given there)

ideas.what: Condition 2: Θ lifts to fundamental groupoids of all K-defined finite étale covers, equivalently stabilizes all Γ-stable open subgroups.
ideas.modern_name: compatibility with the tower of K-rational covers / Galois-stable open subgroups

ideas.what: Condition 3: Θ' stabilizes kernels of π̂_1(X',x') → π̂_1(Y,f(x')) for K-morphisms to other curves.
ideas.modern_name: functoriality with respect to geometric (non-covering) morphisms; cf. 'tripod' conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pop (finite tripod variants of I/OM); Mochizuki / Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki (tripod synchronization)

ideas.what: Condition 4: compatibility with arbitrary K-morphisms between covers of X, not just X-morphisms, via groupoid maps on J = I'_1 ∩ f^{-1}(I'_2).
ideas.modern_name: action on the category of dessins / tower with all morphisms; I/OM-type conditions

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates, before Drinfeld's GT and long before Pop's work, a strategy close to the I/OM program. G_K is to be cut out of Aut π̂_1(U_{0,3}) by compatibility with all K-defined covers and with all K-morphisms between them, especially morphisms NOT over the base, and with morphisms to other curves. Pop's finite-tripod theorem is close to this list, but proving that such conditions actually characterize G_Q is a later result.
missed.quote: f un morphisme X'_1 → X'_2 (pas nécessairement un X-morphisme !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The page documents Grothendieck's priority for the 'compatibility with all morphisms of the tower' formulation now associated with Ihara/Oda–Matsumoto/Pop. Condition 3 (kernel stability for maps to arbitrary curves) is a concrete variant one could compare with tripod-type conditions.

missed.claim: He states that conditions 2–4 are not the 'really natural' ones and that the real point is necessary and sufficient conditions. He never settles which finite subset suffices, e.g. whether condition 1 plus conditions from M_{0,4}, M_{0,5} suffice.
missed.quote: Le point [...] est réellement de dégager conditions néc. et suff. qui permettent de caractériser les Θ provenant de Γ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This remains open in the GT setting (is G_Q = GT?). Variants with richer compatibility conditions have only partly been settled (Pop, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki).

deep.surprise_reason: The overall program is known from the Esquisse. However, this explicit list of conditions (lifting to K-covers, kernel stability under maps to other curves, compatibility with non-X-morphisms between covers), written around 1978–84, anticipates the I/OM / Pop finite-tripod style characterizations. It is not, to my knowledge, published in this form. It is not a finished result, though.
transcription_corrections: 'X'|I' denotes the inverse image (fibre) of I in X'.
In condition 3, 'π̂_1(X', x) → π̂_1(Y, f(x))' should read with x' (the manuscript itself has x).
'(x ∈ X_K ∪ I)' in condition 2 refers to a base point either K-rational or in I.
Line before 'sous l'action': likely 'des sous-groupes ouverts de π_1(X,x) ... stables sous l'action de Γ'.
Last lines likely read: 'est compatible avec les actions prolongées de Θ sur les groupoïdes précédents (modulo l'indétermination de cette action, s'il y a lieu ... cf 2.)'.
